description: Make a photo look old on iPhone: fade, yellowing, dust, stains, creases and light leaks that make a new picture look like a print kept in a shoebox for years.
h1: How to make a photo look old on iPhone
card_summary: Fade, yellowing, dust, creases and leaks: turn a new photo into a print from the shoebox.
quick_answer: An old photo is faded, yellowed and physically worn. In Halatto, pick a warm film look first, then open Aging and start from the Shoebox or Faded print preset. Raise Fade and Yellowing, add some Unevenness, then dust, stains or creases and a light leak at the edge. The Photos app can only lower contrast and warm the color; it cannot add wear.
intro: "Vintage" covers two different things: the color of old film, and the damage time does to a print. The best old-photo effects combine both.
This guide shows the settings to change and the order to apply them so the result looks aged, not just filtered.

sections.heading: The signs of an old photo
list: Fade: blacks turn gray and contrast drops.
Yellowing: whites drift warm and the whole print turns amber.
Uneven color: one side faded more than the other.
Wear: dust specks, stains, creases and bent corners.
Light leaks: a warm glow bleeding in from the edge of the film.

sections.heading: Making it look old for free in Photos
paragraphs: In Photos, tap Edit, then lower Contrast and Saturation, raise Warmth and Shadows, and lower Black Point. You can also try the Silvertone filter for a black and white print. This fades the photo, but there is no way to add dust, stains, creases or leaks.

steps.heading: Step by step: an old photo in Halatto

items.name: Open the photo and pick a look
items.text: Choose a warm film look (Snap Gold, Titan 38) or Mju 35 for black and white.

items.name: Age the print
items.text: Open Aging, tap Shoebox, Faded print or the 70s preset, then fine-tune Fade, Sunlight, Yellowing and Unevenness.

items.name: Add wear
items.text: Add film grain, dust, stains and creases until the print looks handled.

items.name: Add a light leak
items.text: Open Light Leak, choose Edge and Orange or Golden, keep Amount low.

items.name: Save
items.text: Save the photo, or save the edit as a recipe for a whole album.

tips.heading: Tips
items: Age the color before you add wear; damage on a modern-looking color gives it away.
Creases look real on portraits and family photos, less so on landscapes.
Add a date stamp from the right era to finish the story.
Compare with the before/after divider to avoid overdoing it.

faq.question: How do I make a picture look 100 years old?
faq.answer: Use a black and white look like Mju 35, raise Fade and Yellowing for a sepia tone, add dust, stains and creases, and drop the date stamp.

faq.question: Can I make a photo look old and scratched?
faq.answer: Halatto has no separate scratch tool. For a worn, handled print, use Aging with dust, creases and stains, raise Fade and Yellowing, and add a light leak. Together they give the marks and wear of an old print.

faq.question: Can I undo the aging later?
faq.answer: Yes. Halatto keeps your edits, so you can reopen the photo and change or remove any effect.

faq.question: Does this damage the original photo?
faq.answer: No. The edited version is saved; the original stays in your library.
